before.exam_tip_html:
On a 6-mark Explain question about Sikh beliefs about human life or mukti, always cite the Guru Granth Sahib as your source of authority — for example, reference the five khands from the Guru Granth Sahib, or Guru Nanak’s teaching on God’s grace (nadar). The mark scheme requires a named sacred writing or source of religious belief and teaching. Use “the Guru Granth Sahib teaches...” inside one of your reasons. The top band needs two reasons, each developed, not one.

Watch out for the karma misconception: do NOT write that karma in Sikhism means fate or destiny. The mark scheme rewards students who explain that karma is moral causation (intentional actions produce consequences) and that God’s grace can overcome even a heavy burden of karma. This is the kind of specific, accurate knowledge that separates Mastering from Developing answers.

On any question about sewa, make sure you distinguish the three types using their Punjabi terms: tan (physical), man (mental) and dhan (material). Answers that describe sewa only as “helping others” or “volunteering” miss the theological depth — sewa is understood as worship of God, not simply philanthropy. The mark scheme rewards the explanation that serving another person is serving God’s divine light within them.

For the 6-mark Explain question, name the Guru Granth Sahib as your source of authority. You can reference the GGS teaching that serving humanity and serving God are not separate acts, or its teaching that the company of God-centred people strengthens a person’s faith. That counts as a named source. To reach the top band you still need two reasons, each developed.
